sentences.text: 1. This intra-court appeal by the appellant is directed against the order dated 19.11.2018 passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court [the Writ Court] in OWP No. 1674/2018 titled "Mohd. Shafi Bhat versus State of J&K & Ors".

entities.text: Mohd. Shafi Bhat versus State of J&K & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The impugned order reads as under.

"Learned counsel for the respondents submits that in case adequate funds are available, the same will be released in favour of the petitioner on account of acquisition of his land within a period of three weeks.

In view of the aforesaid, submission, this petition is, accordingly, disposed of along with connected IA."
2.
The impugned order is assailed by the appellant primarily on the ground that the Writ Court has not determined the actual controversy raised in the writ petition.

It is submitted that the short grievance that was projected by the appellant before the Writ Court was that his land falling CM No.
Mohd. Shafi Bhat vs State Of J&K & Ors on 7 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95431354/
1 1739/2019 [1/2019] under Khasra no. 529, 490 min, 516, 601/531, 637/531 measuring 100 kanals had been forcibly taken possession of by the respondents.

The appellant had, in essence, prayed for a direction to the respondents to initiate the process of acquisition for acquiring the subject land in accordance with law so that the petitioner received a just and fair compensation for his land.

This issue, which was directly raised for consideration, was not taken note of by the Writ Court and in terms of the order impugned, the writ petition was disposed of by providing that in case the additional funds were available with the respondents the same would be released in favour of the appellant herein on account of acquisition of his land within a period of three weeks.

3. The appeal came up for consideration before this Court on 27.03.2019 when this Court, while issuing notice to the respondents, also directed that the status report regarding the position of the acquisition of the subject land and the payment of compensation to the appellant shall be filed within a period of two weeks.
The matter has thereafter remained pending and has been adjourned on several occasions so as to provide opportunity to the respondents to file the requisite report.
4. The Collector Land Acquisition as also the other respondents have filed their respective objections.

In the reply affidavit filed by the Collector Land Acquisition, (SHEP), Ramban ["the Collector"], it has been brought to the notice of this Court that the acquisition proceedings which were initiated on the indent of Chief Engineer, Sawalakote Hydroelectric Project, Ramban ["indenting department"] have culminated into issuance of a tentative award under Section 11 of the J&K State Land Acquisition Act.

It is submitted by the Collector that further process could not be CM No. 1739/2019 [1/2019] undertaken due to the failure of the indenting department to provide requisite funds for disbursal of the compensation to the rightful owners.

From the reply affidavit filed by the Collector, it comes out that the notification under Section 4(1) of the Jammu & Kashmir Land Acquisition Act Svt. 1990 ["State Land Acquisition Act"] was issued by the Collector on 27.02.2018 and a declaration under Section 6 was made by the Commissioner Secretary to the Government Department of Revenue vide notification 197-Rev (LAJ) of 2018 dated 25.04.2018.

entities.text: Jammu & Kashmir Land Acquisition Act Svt. 1990
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This was followed by notification under Section 9 and 9-A of the State Land Acquisition Act.

Since,
as per the Collector, the land owners/interested persons did not file objections, as such, the Collector proceeded to workout the compensation and make the tentative assessment of the compensation in terms of Section 11 of the State Land Acquisition.

He further submits that he has already passed a tentative award vide no. 609/18/SVP dated 12.02.2019.
5.
The Collector has not in so many words given the reasons as to why the final award has not been passed so far.

However, from the reading of his reply affidavit, it clearly transpires that he could not do so in view of non-availability of the requisite funds to be provided by the indenting department for disbursal of the compensation to the rightful owners.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record, we are of the considered opinion that in view of the subsequent developments i.e. passing of tentative award on 12.02.2019, which has not been finalized, the relief claimed by the appellant in the writ petition is partially rendered infructuous.

sentences.text: Indisputably, the process for land acquisition came to be initiated by the Collector by issuance of Section 4(1) notification vide no. 205/12/SKP dated 27.02.2018, whereby the objections were invited from the interested persons to the proposed acquisition.

Since none of the interested persons filed objections with regard to the acquisition of land in question within the stipulated period, the case was referred to the Commissioner Secretary to the Government for issuance of requisite declaration under Section 6 and 7 of the Act.
8. The Commissioner Secretary to the Government Revenue Department vide its notification dated 25.04.2018 issued the requisite declaration that the said land was required for public purpose.
As is provided, under Section 11-B, the Collector is under an obligation to make an award under Section 11 within a period of two years from the date of publication of declaration.
It further provides that if no award is made within such period, the entire proceedings for acquisition of land would lapse.

From reading of Section 11-B of the State Land Acquisition Act, it clearly transpires that the Collector is obliged to make the award in terms of Section 11(4) of the State Land Acquisition Act within a stipulated period of two years from the date of publication of the declaration.

For facility of reference, relevant extract of Section 11 of the State Land Acquisition Act is reproduced hereunder:-
"11-B. Period within which an award shall be made.--

The Collector shall make an award under section 11within a period of two years from the date of the publication of the declaration and if no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for the acquisition of land shall lapse : Provided that in case where the said declaration has been published before the commencement of the State Land Acquisition CM No.
1739/2019 [1/2019] (Amendment) Act, 1997, the award shall be made within a period of two years from such commencement.

Explanation :--In computing the period of two years referred to in this section, the period during which any action or proceedings to be taken in pursuance of the said declaration is stayed by an order of a court, shall be excluded.]
9.

In the instant case the Collector has made the tentative assessment of the compensation in terms of Section 11(1) (b) of the State Land Acquisition Act but has not proceeded further to make the award which was required of him under Sub-Section 4 of Section 11.
Since the declaration under Section 6 was published on 25.04.2018 and therefore the Collector in terms of Section 11(b) was under an obligation to make his award by or before 24.04.2020.
This has, however, not happened in the instant case.
We are in the year 2023 and the award in terms of Section 11(4) is yet to be passed by the respondents.
10. Mr. Amit Gupta, appearing for Sawalakote Hydroelectric Project- respondents 2 & 4, submits that the entire project has been handed over to NHPC.
We fail to understand how this will change the complexion of the case.
The subject land is yet not acquired and there is no question of this land having been transferred to the project.
That being the position, the subject land shall be deemed to be in possession and actual control of SHEP i.e. respondent Nos. 2 to 4.

sentences.text: It is, thus, a foregone conclusion that the acquisition proceedings in the instant case, which came to be initiated in terms of Section 4 of notification dated 27.02.2018 and regarding which the declaration in terms of Section 6 was issued on 25.04.2018, have lapsed w.e.f. 24.04.2020.
We, therefore, allow this appeal and set aside the judgment of learned Single Judge.

Consequently, we allow the writ petition by holding that the proceedings of land acquisition initiated by the respondents have lapsed in terms of Section 11-B and therefore cannot be permitted to proceed further.
The land acquisition proceedings qua the land of the appellant are quashed.

13. The respondents, however, are well within their right to initiate fresh land acquisition proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, if they require the land belonging to the petitioner for any public purpose.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

sentences.text: The decision in this regard shall be taken by the respondents within a period of four weeks from the date a copy of this order is served upon them.
It is made clear that in case the said land is not required by the indenting department, the same shall be returned to rightful owners within four weeks thereafter.
( (Javed Iqbal Wani) (Sanjeev Kumar)
